text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated CUDA OOMs on decoder-streaming pods in us-west-2. Spike started ~14:11 UTC, affected node pool: decode-prod-usw2-a. Error: "CUDA out of memory while allocating tensor" repeated across ~40% of pods in past 5m. Suspected trigger: runaway streaming / max_tokens not clamped from some client requests. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): seeing the page, jumping in. Checking dashboards now. Can someone post the top error logs pls?

kevin (eng-runtime): logs attached from one crash loop: ```
E 2026-03-15T14:12:23Z decoder.cpp:511 CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY while allocating 4294967296 bytes
E 2026-03-15T14:12:23Z decode_loop: attempted generation length 65536 > configured token budget
``` Noticed a handful of requests with client max_tokens=100000 in access logs.

ryan (sre): that matches the trend — request distribution shows a tail at 50k+ tokens over last 10m. Runtime used to enforce server-side clamp but the v2 rollout removed the clamp env by mistake. Reproducer: send streaming request with headers: `X-Client-Max-Tokens: 100000` -> decoder accepts and tries to allocate KV cache.

carol (product-sre): customer-impact? alice any support reports?

alice (support): two customers reported increased 503s and streaming disconnects since 14:10 UTC: cust-A (low traffic) and cust-B (high concurrency). I have a ticket open for cust-B, flagged as P1.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) apply hotpatch to reinstate server-side max_tokens clamp (2048) 2) temporarily route streaming traffic to the quantized fallback pool (lower memory) for us-west-2 3) enable short-term per-pod request throttling to shed large requests. Doing (1) now.

kevin (eng-runtime): hotpatch command (in case useful): ```bash
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/decoder MAX_TOKENS_SERVER_CAP=2048
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/decoder
``` This will cause rolling restart; each pod will come up with clamp in ENV and check incoming requests.

deploy-bot: deploy/decoder annotated with MAX_TOKENS_SERVER_CAP=2048. Starting rollout: 6 pods -> 1-by-1 restart.

ryan (sre): while rollout happens, I'll enable a traffic rule to route new streaming sessions to decode-fallback-usw2 pool: ```
# quick routing patch
redwoodctl route modify --pool decode-default-usw2 ---> decode-fallback-usw2 --percent 100 --reason "OOM mitigation"
``` Doing now.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for deploy/decoder (6/6 pods updated). Health checks OK.

kevin (eng-runtime): logs post-patch show OOMs dropping immediately. Sample: ```
W 2026-03-15T14:18:03Z runtime: saw client max_tokens=100000 clamped to 2048 by env MAX_TOKENS_SERVER_CAP
INFO 14:18:04 healthcheck: pod healthy
```

maria (oncall): customer impact: 503 rate dropped from 6% -> 0.6% in 10m window. cust-B still had some errors during the restart window but stable now. Marking incident as mitigated; continuing monitoring for 60m.

carol (product-sre): follow-ups: 1) add integration test to prevent removing MAX_TOKENS_SERVER_CAP on rollouts 2) implement server-side hard clamp in runtime (not only env) with telemetry 3) add a circuit-breaker to refuse single-request token budgets > 10k for streaming endpoints by default 4) postmortem and customer outreach doc.

ryan (sre): creating pager postmortem and assigning owners. Also will add an automated alert for token budget tail (p99 > 4096) so we page earlier.

alice (support): I'll send a customer-facing summary for cust-B and offer a follow-up call. Tagging support-runbook.

maria (oncall): handing off monitoring to kevin for next 2 hours. If OOM rate stays low, we'll close. Kept logs and a short runbook note under incident-2367000001 in /incidents. :white_check_mark:

kevin (eng-runtime): taking handoff. I'll keep an eye on OOMs and traffic routing. If we see >1% request drop rate or OOMs spike, I'll escalate to infra and consider capacity increase.

incident-bot: Incident state changed to MITIGATED by maria. Timeline and logs archived to incident-2367000001. Reminder: open postmortem draft and assign follow-ups.

maria (oncall): quick summary for the postmortem: root cause = v2 rollout removed server-side max_tokens env clamp leading to acceptance of extreme token budgets; symptom = GPU OOMs on decode streaming pods causing request drops; mitigation = env hotpatch + routing to low-memory fallback pool; long-term fixes assigned.
